## 📘 Exam Structure

-   Available all day in Blackboard (from morning until 11:59 p.m.)
-   You may begin the exam at any time during that window
-   Once started, you must complete it in one sitting — **1 hour** time limit
-   Question types:
    -   Term definitions
    -   Multiple choice
    -   True/False
    -   Fill-in-the-blank
    -   Short-answer (open-ended)
-   Total points: **110** (including bonus)
-   **Open-book and open-note**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📗 Chapter 1: Introduction & Basics

-   What is Java? (general-purpose, object-oriented, platform-independent)
-   Structure of a Java program: `class`, `main` method, statements
-   Output: `System.out.println()`
-   Variables: declaration, types (`int`, `double`, `String`, `boolean`)
-   Assignment and initialization
-   Comments: `//` (single-line), `/* ... */` (multi-line)
-   Basic arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`
-   Input using `Scanner` (if covered)
-   Naming conventions: identifiers, case sensitivity

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📘 Chapter 2: Variables, Data Types, and Expressions

-   Primitive types: `int`, `double`, `char`, `boolean`
-   Type conversion: implicit (widening), explicit (casting)
-   Constants: `final` keyword
-   Expressions and operator precedence
-   String concatenation
-   Input with `Scanner`: `nextInt()`, `nextDouble()`, `nextLine()`
-   Common errors: type mismatch, input mismatch

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📙 Chapter 3: Selections (Decision Making)

-   Relational operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
-   Logical operators: `&&`, `||`, `!`
-   `if` statements: basic, nested, `if-else`, `if-else-if`
-   `switch` statement: syntax, `case`, `break`, `default`
-   Boolean expressions and truth tables
-   Common patterns: grading, min/max, comparisons
-   Input validation
-   Short-circuit evaluation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✅ General Tips

-   Know how to write and trace simple Java programs
-   Be able to explain and use variables, data types, and operators
-   Understand how to get input and produce output
-   Practice writing selection statements (`if`, `switch`)
-   Be ready to debug and fix common syntax errors

------------------------------------------------------------------------

We’ll thoroughly review these concepts in class this week — bring your questions and stay engaged. You’ve got this!
